title: Philadelphia Fed Fourth Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters — 10:00 a.m. ET, the oldest US macro consensus (1968) and the only tracked event on its date, measured across 145 releases to move nothing
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/survey-of-professional-forecasters/spf-release-dates.txt — the SURVEY'S OWN 'Dates of Previous Surveys' file, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 8,298 bytes), listing the true deadline and news-release date of every SPF since 1990Q2 (146 quarters). This discharges the proposal's task (a) with a stronger surface than a release page: the date is now DERIVED from the publisher's own 36-year cadence record, not merely enumerated. THE CONSTRUCTION RULE: the deadline is the Tuesday (occasionally Monday) of the second week of the quarter's middle month, and the release is exactly 3 BUSINESS DAYS later once weekends AND the Veterans Day federal holiday are excluded — 40 of 59 quarters since 2012 land on exactly 3 business days, 53 of 59 on 3 or 4, and both larger outliers are the government-shutdown quarters the file itself footnotes (2013Q4, 2019Q1). Applied to Q4 2026: the second Tuesday of November 2026 is Tue 2026-11-10; three business days later, skipping Wed 2026-11-11 (Veterans Day), is Mon 2026-11-16. This also EXPLAINS the one apparent anomaly a naive reader would trip on — Q1/Q2/Q3 have released on a Friday 45 times out of 45 since 2012 with zero exceptions, while Q4 is a Monday in 15 of 21 years since 2005. There is no separate Q4 rule: Veterans Day sits inside the Q4 window and pushes the same 3-business-day turnaround from Friday to Monday. A session extrapolating 'the SPF always prints on a Friday' would have predicted 2026-11-13 and been wrong. Corroborated by the bank's calendar endpoint (philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes), whose embedded structured data enumerates the full 2026 SPF schedule as four rows all at 10:00 a.m. — 'First Quarter | Mar 6', 'Second Quarter | May 15', 'Third Quarter | Aug 14', and verbatim 'Fourth Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters | Nov 16 2026 | 10:00 a.m.' — whose three PAST 2026 rows match the release-dates file exactly, which is what makes the fourth row trustworthy. Filed estimate on two counts, NEITHER of which is doubt about the date: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own release schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16.from-philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25.json, filed 2026-09-09) and discharged all three tasks it assigned. (a) DATE — re-verified and, better, derived; see `source`. (b) IMPACT TIER — the proposal explicitly left open that 'an argument exists that a national consensus release deserves medium'. That argument is REFUTED by measurement, not declined by taste. Absolute close-to-close moves on SPF news-release days versus every other day, joined from the publisher's own release-date file to FRED daily series: 10-year TIPS breakeven T10YIE, n=95 release days 2003-2026, mean |change| 0.0223 vs 0.0230 on all other days (ratio 0.97, Welch t=-0.34); 5-year breakeven T5YIE, ratio 1.01, t=+0.09; VIX close, n=145 release days 1990-2026, ratio 1.04, t=+0.36; 10-year Treasury DGS10, n=145, ratio 1.04, t=+0.53. The series most directly comparable to what the SPF publishes — a 10-year inflation expectation — moves LESS on SPF days than on an average day. LOW is now measured rather than inherited. (c) HAS IT EVER MOVED A TAPE — no, and the mechanism is the survey's own numbers. The SPF's 10-year annual-average headline CPI projection has a standard deviation of 0.157pp across 95 quarters since 2003, a mean quarterly change of 0.062pp, and a full 24-year range of 2.03-2.95. The market's own 10-year breakeven over the identical span has sd 0.392 and range 0.04-3.02 — 2.5x the volatility across a band 3.2x as wide — and the correlation of their QUARTERLY CHANGES is 0.156, effectively zero. A number that moves six basis points a quarter cannot surprise a market that moves the same concept by forty. The SPF's near-term forecast does move (1-year CPI sd 0.395, mean quarterly change 0.153pp) but that is precisely the content weekly sell-side consensus already supplies. WHAT EARNS THE ROW instead is scheduling. Nothing else on this calendar is dated 2026-11-16 — the SPF would be the only tracked event that day, the exact inverse of its proposer PIES, which releases 90 minutes after PCE. And the DERIVED collection deadline, Tue 2026-11-10, is the same date as cpi-2026-11-10 (high, confirmed) and us-china-tariff-truce-expiry-2026-11-10 (high, estimate): whether the Q4 panel's information set contains the October CPI print and the truce outcome turns on hours within a single day that the publisher does not disclose. That is the one genuinely unresolved fact about this print, and it is a reading rule, not a trade. Corridor: 2 days before fomc-minutes-2026-11-18 (medium, confirmed), 12 days before fomc-blackout-start-2026-11-28 (medium, confirmed), 23 days before fomc-2026-12-09. The proposal's framing that it is 'the last published professional consensus before the December FOMC blackout' is narrowed here: philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25 also precedes the blackout, so the honest claim is that the SPF is the last NATIONAL forecaster consensus before it. SHUTDOWN SENSITIVITY IS DOCUMENTED BY THE PUBLISHER, not inferred: the release-dates file footnotes that the 2026Q1, 2019Q1, 2013Q4 and 1996Q1 surveys were all delayed by federal government shutdowns, and that 2025Q4 shipped without historical jump-off values because agencies were dark from 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-12. This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
